gaps: FOMC release times: the Fed's press-release page prints a time only from 2016-01-27 on. For 2010-01-27 through 2011-03-15 (10 statements), 2012-03-13 and 2012-08-01, the 14:15 ET time is not printed on the statement page; it is the standing schedule stated in the Fed's own 2011-03-24 announcement (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20110324a.htm) and the NY Fed post (https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2018/11/the-pre-fomc-announcement-drift-more-recent-evidence/). Each row's note says which basis applies.
2010-11-03: printed release time absent on the Fed press release; 14:15 ET taken from a secondary Fed/NY Fed statement of the standing schedule
2010-12-14: printed release time absent on the Fed press release; 14:15 ET taken from a secondary Fed/NY Fed statement of the standing schedule
2013-01-30: time 14:00 rests on the NY Fed post, not a Fed-printed time

2010-05-09 (Sunday) unscheduled FOMC statement on dollar liquidity swap lines (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/press/monetary/20100509a.htm) is not a rate decision and falls on a weekend; excluded. No other unscheduled FOMC statements exist in 2010-01..2019-04 (fomchistorical pages list conference calls 2010-10-15, 2011-08-01, 2011-11-28, 2013-10-16, 2014-03-04 without policy statements).

BLS archive pages (bls.gov returns 403 to scripts) were not fetched individually; each source_url is the release-archive file name taken from BLS's own index, read through the Wayback Machine copy https://web.archive.org/web/2020/https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/cpi.htm and .../empsit.htm (copies of the BLS pages of 2020-11-25 and 2020-12-31). Per-URL HTTP 200 checks were not completed.
